title: Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: Classic creamy Italian mushroom risotto
excerpt: A deeply savoury risotto made from a combination of fresh and dried mushrooms, built slowly over 20 minutes with warm stock and finished with butter and parmesan. The dried mushrooms provide intensity that fresh mushrooms alone cannot.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto ai funghi is one of the most celebrated risotto preparations in northern Italian cooking, particularly associated with Piedmont and Lombardy. The technique for risotto, adding warm stock ladle by ladle while stirring constantly, was codified in northern Italian cooking over centuries. Porcini mushrooms, fresh in autumn and dried year-round, are the classic choice; the soaking water from dried porcini is added to the stock to deepen the flavour.

recipeTools.notes: Wide, heavy-based pan for even heat.

content.text: The dried mushrooms provide what fresh mushrooms cannot: a concentrated, almost meaty depth. Soak them in hot water for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid and strain it through a sieve lined with kitchen paper to remove any grit. This soaking liquid goes into the stock. The final step, mantecatura, is beating cold butter and parmesan into the finished risotto off the heat until the whole pan becomes creamy and cohesive.

items.preparation: soaked in 250 ml hot water for 20 min

content.text: Drain the porcini, squeezing well, and chop roughly. Strain the soaking liquid and add it to the warm stock. Fry the fresh mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat until golden, 5 minutes. Set aside.

In the same pan over medium heat, add the remaining oil and 20 g of butter. Cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 2 minutes. Add the porcini and stir for 1 minute. Add the rice and toast, stirring, for 2 minutes. Add the wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the warm stock a ladleful at a time, stirring after each addition and waiting until each is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20 minutes. The rice is done when it is al dente and the risotto flows slowly.

Remove from the heat. Add the remaining cold butter and the parmesan. Beat vigorously until the risotto is creamy. Fold in the fried mushrooms and parsley. Season. Remove the thyme sprigs. Rest for 2 minutes, then serve immediately.
